//: Things no netlist format records: which nets are an I2C bus, and which pins must never float. Each is a rule that was previously only written in prose.
//physics: Facts about the world that no netlist records: what each rail actually carries and sits at. A rail with max_current_a = null is REPORTED as needing a measurement, never assumed safe — an unchecked rail must not look like a passing one.

physics.//i2c_bus_capacitance_pf: A 15 cm ribbon is ~6-10 pF, two PCB fan-outs ~10-20 pF, plus device pin capacitance. 50 pF is the defensible estimate; fast-mode's entire budget is 400 pF.

MOTOR6V.//max_current_a: 1.5 A is the L9110S's own limit, NOT a measurement of this motor. Copper sized for what the driver can pass is sufficient whatever the motor wants, because the driver is in series with it. The unmeasured stall current decides whether the DRIVER is right - it does not change the trace width.
MOTOR6V.//resistor_currents: CurrentShunt is stated as an UPPER BOUND, not a measurement: 1.5 A, the L9110S's own limit (see GND's //CurrentShunt). It is 0.1 ohm in the motor's ground return, so its current IS the motor current — the one number this project has never measured (STATUS.md, next bench task). Until 2026-10-01 it was left unstated so the check would keep asking; that kept the commit gate red on this one line, and every commit skipped the gate. The PO ruled for the bound (spark retro R8.1). Replace it with the measured stall current the day a meter has been on the motor.

GND.//max_current_a: 1.5 A is the L9110S's own limit, NOT a measurement of this motor. Copper sized for what the driver can pass is sufficient whatever the motor wants, because the driver is in series with it. The unmeasured stall current decides whether the DRIVER is right - it does not change the trace width.
GND.//served_by_pour: GND carries the motor return AND every signal return, so a single max_current_a is not true of the whole net - a button's ground does not see 1.5 A. The return is a copper pour, which a trace-width rule cannot size, so the check reports it as unverified rather than pretending either way.
GND.//resistor_currents: Each 100 k pulldown carries 3.3 V / 100 k = 33 uA while its wake input is driven high: 0.1 uW. Stated so the rule can run rather than refuse (spark P34).
GND.//CurrentShunt: The motor's whole return current passes through it, so its worst case is the rail's: 1.5 A, the L9110S's own limit rather than a measurement of this motor. 1.5^2 * 0.1 = 0.225 W against a 2512's 1 W. Comfortable - but it is 0.15 V of sense signal at full current, which is the number the stall detector actually reads, and it is why the shunt is 0.1 ohm and not larger: a bigger shunt reads more easily and steals more of the motor's supply. The bound has margin: a 1 W, 0.1 ohm part holds sqrt(1/0.1) = 3.16 A, twice it.

V33.//max_current_a: The DFR0534 plus the ESP32. An estimate, not a measurement - the module's idle draw has never been measured.
V33.//resistor_currents: The current a netlist cannot record. Each 2.2 k I2C pull-up carries 3.3 V / 2.2 k = 1.5 mA while the bus is held low: 5 mW in an 0603 rated 100.
V33.//pullup_currents: Worst case is the line held hard low: 3.3 V / 2.2k = 1.5 mA for the I2C pair, 3.3 V / 100k = 33 uA for the two wake-input holds. The I2C pair is also the sinking current the bus masters must handle, and 1.5 mA is well inside the 3 mA every device here allows.
